result.title: IsoVRBench: Video Reward Modeling Without Human Feedback
result.summary: Video reward models are trained and evaluated on human preferences between videos that often differ simultaneously on properties such as prompt alignment, visual fidelity, motion, and generator identity. As a result, aggregate accuracy does not reveal which video properties a reward model can reliably distinguish. We construct preference pairs by controlled interventions that change one property of a generated video while holding the rest fixed. The resulting pairs, by construction, provide preferences for how the videos differ along a specific dimension, without requiring any human annotation. We propose IsoVRBench, a video generation reward modeling benchmark of 8,000 such pairs across eight interventions, and show that state-of-the-art models separate broad quality differences between generators but miss important features such as temporal order. The best reward model reaches only 60.8% on reordered frames against 100% for humans, and rankings on existing benchmarks do not predict this failure. Using the synthetic isolated intervation pairs as training data leads to 1) IsoVRM, a reward model outperforming its counterpart trained with a larger human labeled preference dataset by 3.8 points on VBench-2.0, 2) IsoWan, the video generator post-trained with IsoVRM, outperforming its human-data counterpart in human preferences, and 3) gains that stack when combined with human data. Because intervention pairs are automatically generated rather than collected, the benchmark and training data can be easily extended as generators evolve.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 IsoVRBench：用只改变单一属性的受控干预自动生成 8,000 对视频偏好对，诊断视频奖励模型能否区分具体视觉属性，并据此训练奖励模型 IsoVRM 与生成器 IsoWan。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单属性受控干预 + 自动生成偏好监督」的思路可能可供核查，用于诊断 LVR 内部状态是否保留特定视觉属性（如时序、运动），或作为免人工标注的属性判别训练信号；但论文对象是视频生成的奖励模型，与 VLM 推理期状态生成无直接联系。
